title: Embedding quantization meta-benchmark and calibration run orchestration
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Goal: Build an end-to-end orchestration and validation run for INT8/FP16 embedding quantization profiles that combines a meta-benchmark across representative corpora, automated calibration jobs, and cosine-similarity drift detectors. The outcome is an operational artifact (calibration job + metrics + gating decision) that can be used by model-onboarding, runtime, and ops to safely release quantized embedding profiles to production. Scope includes: sample selection strategy, per-layer and per-channel scale estimation exports, offline accept/reject criteria using cosine similarity distributions, a nightly recalibration pipeline, and alerting for production drift.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible meta-benchmark suite runs end-to-end for 5 representative corpora (web, wiki, product-catalog, internal-knowledge, chat-logs) and produces per-profile metrics within the CI artifact store.

Automated calibration pipeline produces INT8 and FP16 profile artifacts and a human-readable summary with suggested fallback (FP16) and per-profile performance delta (avg cosine, 99th percentile loss).

Cosine-similarity drift detector produces baseline distribution, an automatically computed acceptance gate, and an alerting rule that fires when the weekly median cosine declines by > 0.015 or 95th percentile loss increases beyond configured threshold.
Runbook steps for ops to promote or rollback a quantized profile are documented and linked in the PR; a simulated rollback is exercised in staging.
Nightly recalibration job is scheduled, runs reliably for one week, and uploads result artifacts to the metrics store with per-run hashes and provenance metadata.
Benchmarking results show tokenized embedding generation latency change < 5% and service-level throughput impact measured in dedicated staging clusters before promotion.

notes: Design decisions: use stratified sampling by corpus and shard by embedding length buckets (short/medium/long) to avoid bias; compute per-corpus weighted aggregate and expose per-corpus deltas. Operationally we will require two consecutive nightly passes within gate before auto-promotion. Fallback strategy: if INT8 candidate fails gate, fallback to profile tagged FP16-compatible with reduced batching recommendation.
ops_runbook_summary: Promote flow: (1) calibrate on staging with same corpus weight file used in onboarding; (2) run meta-benchmark and record metrics; (3) verify drift detector result is within gate; (4) create release artifact and tag model profile; (5) start canary at 1% traffic for 24h with latency and quality guards; (6) promote to 10% then 100% if stable. Rollback: revert profile tag and re-route requests to FP16 profile; open incident runbook and notify customer success if customer-impacting.
